Contrast listed as an omnibus within-group test; the record does not indicate this is one of the permitted contrast types (problem-solving > baseline, demand manipulation, untrained>trained, type>type, or phase>phase). GLOBAL_I3 (permitted contrast types) is not satisfied.
Stimuli/contrast concern virtual navigation, not numerical problem solving. Missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Stimuli/contrast concern navigation, not verbal problem solving. Missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.

Although the study is about navigation, this particular analysis is an omnibus contrast whose mapping to a permitted problem-solving contrast is not indicated in the record (GLOBAL_I3 not met for this specific analysis). Missing GLOBAL_I3.
This contrast is an omnibus test, not a manipulation of demand/difficulty; missing LOGICAL_REASONING_I1 and GLOBAL_I3.

Customer-driven route planning > coasting is a within-group, whole-brain activation contrast comparing a goal-directed navigation/planning condition to a low-activity baseline; meets voxelwise group map (GLOBAL_I1), task-based problem solving (GLOBAL_I2), permitted contrast type (problem solving > baseline, GLOBAL_I3), healthy group (GLOBAL_I4), and stereotactic reporting (GLOBAL_I5).
Contrast involves navigation stimuli, not numerical problem solving; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Stimuli are navigational/visuospatial, not verbal problem stimuli; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.

Customer-driven route planning is a spatial navigation problem-solving task (goal-directed route planning); meets GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3, GLOBAL_I4, GLOBAL_I5 and VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
This contrast compares task > baseline rather than manipulating demand/complexity; does not meet LOGICAL_REASONING_I1 (no difficulty manipulation).

Contrast compares two phases of customer-driven route planning (initial goal > switch) — a within-domain phase comparison qualifies under GLOBAL_I3 (phase > phase) and meets GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I4, GLOBAL_I5. It represents problem-solving phases, so included.
Contrast concerns spatial navigation phases, not numerical problem solving; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Stimuli are navigational/visuospatial rather than verbal; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.

Initial-goal versus switch phases are distinct navigation planning phases (phase>phase), satisfying VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 in addition to global criteria GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3, GLOBAL_I4, GLOBAL_I5.
This is a phase comparison (initial vs switch) rather than a demand/difficulty manipulation; does not meet LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.

Customer-driven route planning (switch to new goal) > initial goal is a phase comparison of navigation planning (phase>phase), satisfying GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3 (phase contrast), GLOBAL_I4 and GLOBAL_I5.
Contrast is spatial/navigation in nature, not numerical; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Stimuli/contrast are visuospatial navigation phases, not verbal problem solving; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
This contrast isolates navigation planning phases (switch > initial), fitting VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 and global criteria GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3, GLOBAL_I4, GLOBAL_I5.
Phase contrast, not a demand/difficulty manipulation; does not meet LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.

Customer-driven route planning > spontaneous route planning is a within-group type comparison (one problem-solving type > another), which matches GLOBAL_I3 (type>type) and meets GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I4, GLOBAL_I5.
Contrast compares navigation task types (visuospatial), not numerical problem solving; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Stimuli are navigation/visuospatial, not verbal; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.

This is a comparison between two navigation planning types (one planning type > another), satisfying VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 and global criteria GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3, GLOBAL_I4, GLOBAL_I5.
Contrast is type>type (different problem types) rather than a demand/difficulty manipulation; does not meet LOGICAL_REASONING_I1 (and LOGICAL_REASONING_E1 would apply if treating it as type>type).

Conjunction includes customer-driven and spontaneous route-planning contrasts; the underlying contrasts are problem-solving > control/type contrasts, meeting GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3, GLOBAL_I4, GLOBAL_I5 and DOMAIN_GENERAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Conjunction concerns navigational planning contrasts (visuospatial), not numerical stimuli; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Conjunction of navigation planning contrasts — not verbal problem solving; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Conjunction isolates overlap of navigation planning contrasts (route planning), matching VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 and global criteria GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3, GLOBAL_I4, GLOBAL_I5.
This conjunction derives from type/baseline planning contrasts rather than a manipulation of demand/complexity; does not meet LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.

Response to customers' irrelevant statements > coasting appears to reflect processing of verbal/attentional stimuli (listening) rather than goal-directed problem solving; fails GLOBAL_I2 (task-based problem solving) and matches GLOBAL_E4 (non-problem/passive language processing).
Contrast involves listening to speech during navigation, not numerical problem solving; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.

This is listening to customers' irrelevant statements (language comprehension) rather than a verbal problem-solving task; fails VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 and is consistent with VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_E1 (passive language processing).
Contrast indexes response to verbal/irrelevant statements rather than visuospatial navigation planning; fails VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
This contrast is not a manipulation of demand/difficulty; missing LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.

Spontaneous route planning > coasting is a within-group activation contrast isolating goal-directed navigation planning versus baseline; satisfies GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3 (problem-solving > baseline), GLOBAL_I4 and GLOBAL_I5.
This is a navigation/spatial planning contrast, not numerical problem solving; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Stimuli are visuospatial/navigation not verbal problem content; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Spontaneous route planning is a prototypical navigation problem-solving task (VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1) and meets GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3, GLOBAL_I4, GLOBAL_I5.
Contrast is task>baseline rather than a demand manipulation; does not meet LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.

Action planning > coasting isolates planning/execution-related activity during navigation; given the task context (goal-directed navigation where planning actions is part of solving the route), this meets GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3 (problem solving > baseline), GLOBAL_I4, and GLOBAL_I5.
Contrast concerns navigation/action planning, not manipulation of numeric stimuli; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Action planning here is visuomotor/navigation-related rather than verbal problem solving; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Action planning during navigation is part of spatial problem solving and meets VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 along with global criteria (GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3, GLOBAL_I4, GLOBAL_I5).
Contrast is task versus baseline rather than a demand/difficulty manipulation; does not meet LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.

Expectation confirmation > coasting seems to reflect prediction/response processing rather than goal-directed problem solving; the record does not indicate this is a problem-solving contrast (fails GLOBAL_I2).
Contrast concerns expectation-related processing during navigation, not numerical problem solving; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
This contrast reflects expectation processes rather than a verbal problem-solving task; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Expectation confirmation is not clearly a navigation planning/problem-solving process in the record; fails VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1/GLOBAL_I2.
This contrast is not a demand/difficulty manipulation; missing LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.
Expectation violation > coasting indexes surprise/violation detection rather than explicit goal-directed problem solving per the record; fails GLOBAL_I2 (not clearly problem solving).
Contrast concerns expectancy/violation processing in navigation, not numerical problem solving; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Not a verbal problem-solving contrast; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Expectation violation is not clearly a navigation planning/problem solving contrast per the record; fails VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1/GLOBAL_I2.
Not a difficulty manipulation; missing LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.
Expectation epochs > coasting epochs reflects expectation-related processing rather than clear goal-directed problem solving in the record; fails GLOBAL_I2.
This contrast is not numeric problem solving; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Expectation epochs are not described as a verbal problem-solving task; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Expectation epochs are not clearly navigation planning/problem solving per the record; fails VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1/GLOBAL_I2.
Not a demand/difficulty contrast; missing LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.

Visual inspection epochs > coasting epochs appears to index perceptual/inspection processes rather than goal-directed problem solving; fails GLOBAL_I2 and aligns with GLOBAL_E4 (non-problem passive/perceptual processing).
This is a visual/perceptual contrast, not numeric problem solving; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Not a verbal problem-solving contrast; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.

Although visuospatial in stimulus type, 'visual inspection' as described reads as perception/inspection rather than a navigation problem-solving operation; fails VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 (no evidence of goal-directed problem solving in the record).
Not a demand/difficulty manipulation; missing LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.

Monitoring traffic epochs > coasting epochs appears to index vigilance/monitoring rather than explicit goal-directed route planning in the record; GLOBAL_I2 (problem-solving) is not clearly met from the extraction.
Monitoring traffic is not numerical problem solving; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Monitoring traffic is not verbal problem-solving; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.

Although spatial in nature, 'monitoring traffic' is described as an attentional/monitoring epoch rather than active navigation planning per the record; VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 is not clearly satisfied.
Not a demand/difficulty manipulation; missing LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.

Customer-driven route planning > response to customers' irrelevant statements contrasts planning against a non-planning verbal baseline, capturing goal-directed navigation planning; meets GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3 (problem-solving > control), GLOBAL_I4 and GLOBAL_I5.
This contrast compares navigation planning to a verbal baseline and does not involve numerical stimuli; missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Although the contrast uses a verbal baseline, the active condition is navigation planning (visuospatial), not a verbal problem-solving task; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.

Customer-driven route planning versus irrelevant statements isolates navigation planning processes (VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1) and satisfies GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2, GLOBAL_I3, GLOBAL_I4, GLOBAL_I5.
Contrast is planning>baseline type, not a manipulation of difficulty/complexity; does not meet LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.

This is a whole-brain, group-level BOLD activation map (healthy controls) for a goal-directed virtual-maze navigation task (DECIDE > BASELINE). Global criteria (voxelwise whole-brain task map, problem-solving task, permitted contrast type, healthy-group effect, stereotactic reporting) are met, so it qualifies for the domain-general pooled problem-solving target.
Stimuli and task are spatial navigation in a virtual maze, not numerical manipulation. Missing MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 (numerical stimuli/manipulation).
Task uses a pictorial/spatial virtual maze rather than word/sentence/letter stimuli; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 (verbal stimuli and problems).

The task is spatial navigation in a virtual maze (find the goal), which fits VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 (spatial navigation problem solving). Global voxelwise, whole-brain, healthy-group BOLD contrast DECIDE>BASELINE is satisfied.
The contrast is task versus baseline (DECIDE > BASELINE), not a manipulation of problem demand/difficulty. Missing LOGICAL_REASONING_I1 (demand/difficulty contrast).
Does not meet GLOBAL_I4: this is a patient-only (schizophrenia) within-group analysis; the benchmark requires group-level effects in healthy participants. Therefore excluded.
Patient-only group; also stimuli are spatial, not numerical. Missing GLOBAL_I4 (healthy-group effect) and MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Patient-only group; task uses spatial virtual maze rather than verbal stimuli. Missing GLOBAL_I4 and VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Although the task is visuospatial, this analysis is from a schizophrenia patient group and thus fails GLOBAL_I4 (benchmark requires healthy-group effects).
Fails GLOBAL_I4 (not a healthy-group analysis) and does not present a demand/difficulty contrast (missing LOGICAL_REASONING_I1).
This is a between-group contrast (controls > participants with schizophrenia), which is excluded by GLOBAL_E6 (between-group contrasts).
Between-group contrast excluded (GLOBAL_E6); additionally, task is spatial rather than numerical so MATHEMATICAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 is not met.
Between-group contrast excluded by GLOBAL_E6; task also not verbal (VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1 not met).
Despite being a spatial navigation task, this specific analysis is a between-group contrast and thus excluded by GLOBAL_E6.
Between-group contrast excluded (GLOBAL_E6); also not a demand/difficulty contrast (LOGICAL_REASONING_I1 not met).
